Your Docker containers in Gladys, through the REST API of Portainer (CE or
BE 2.x) on your network:

- each container becomes a Gladys device: **running** and **healthy** (its
  Docker healthcheck), **CPU (%)**, **memory** (MB), and **start**, **stop**
  and **restart** buttons;
- each Portainer environment becomes a device with its **containers running**
  and **containers stopped**;
- the **Container stopped or unhealthy** scene trigger.

> **This integration has never been tested against a real Portainer.** This
> first version was written from the Portainer API reference, the Docker
> Engine API and tomaae/homeassistant-portainer, and tested against a fake
> Portainer only. Please report what works and what does not on the Gladys
> forum.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Portainer.io.

## Before you start: a dedicated user and its token

1. In Portainer, **Administration → User-related → Users**, create a user
   `gladys` (Portainer BE: give it the **Read-only user** role on the
   environments Gladys should only watch, **Operator** where it may start and
   stop containers; Portainer CE: add it to a team that has access to these
   environments).
2. Log in as this user, open **My account → Access tokens → Add access
   token**, name it `gladys` and copy the token (it starts with `ptr_`):
   Portainer shows it only once.
3. An administrator token works too, but gives Gladys much more than it needs.

## Configuration

- **Portainer address**: `https://192.168.1.10:9443`. A bare address (without
  `https://`) is read as https on port 9443, Portainer's own. With `https://`
  and no port, the port is 443 (80 for `http://`), like in a browser: that is
  the case of Portainer behind a reverse proxy, whose path is kept
  (`https://example.org/portainer`). Avoid `http://192.168.1.10:9000`: the
  token would cross your network in clear.
- **Access token**: kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent
  only to Portainer, in the `X-API-Key` header (never in an address, never in
  a log, never in the `/data` volume). Paste the token alone: a space or an
  invisible character copied with it is refused with a clear message.
- **Certificate** (https only; with an `http://` address these options are
  refused): by default the certificate of Portainer must come from a known
  authority (Let's Encrypt…). Portainer generates a self-signed one on port
  9443; two ways to accept it:
  - **Accept the self-signed certificate**: trust on first use. A certificate
    valid for the host (known authority) is accepted without a pin.
    Otherwise the certificate seen at the first connection is trusted and
    remembered (in the `/data` volume of the integration): **the token goes
    to whoever answers this first connection**, and again to whoever answers
    the first connection after **Trust the new certificate**. After that, a
    different certificate is refused before the token is sent.
  - **Certificate fingerprint**: safer, the only way to close the first-use
    window: nothing else is ever accepted, not even the first time, not even
    a certificate from a known authority. In your browser, open Portainer,
    click the padlock, show the certificate and copy its SHA-256 fingerprint;
    or run
    `openssl s_client -connect 192.168.1.10:9443 </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256`.
- **Environments**: names or ids, separated by commas; empty, every Docker
  environment the token sees. Edge and Kubernetes environments are left out.
- **Allow starting, stopping and restarting containers**: off by default (see
  Commands).
- **CPU and memory**: every minute (default) to every 10 minutes, or not read.

Then open the **Discovery** tab and create the containers and environments
you want to follow. Only the created containers get their CPU and memory
read.

## Commands

- Off by default: Gladys only reads. Once **Allow starting, stopping and
  restarting containers** is ticked, the **Start**, **Stop** and **Restart**
  buttons act on the container.
- **Running** is a reading, never a switch: Gladys hands every switch to the
  voice assistants (Google Home, Alexa, HomeKit), to MCP and to the "turn
  off" scene actions, so "turn everything off" would stop your containers.
  Use the buttons, from the dashboard or a scene.
- **Never** stopped nor restarted from Gladys, even when allowed:
  - Gladys and its integrations: a label of the Gladys core
    (`io.gladysassistant.…`), an image `gladysassistant/…` or a repository
    named `gladys…`, or a container whose name starts with `gladys`;
  - Portainer and its agent: images `portainer/portainer-ce`, `-ee`,
    `portainer/agent`, or a name starting with `portainer`;
  - any container connected to the Docker socket (`docker.sock`): it manages
    the others (the Gladys core, a socket proxy, Watchtower…);
  - the container of this integration itself.
    Starting them stays possible.
- **Not recognized, so not protected**: the other containers your house
  needs, such as the reverse proxy in front of Portainer or Gladys (Traefik,
  Nginx Proxy Manager, Caddy), your DNS (Pi-hole, AdGuard Home) or the MQTT
  broker Gladys uses (Mosquitto). Stopping one of them can cut Gladys from
  Portainer, or your whole network: leave the commands off, or give the token
  user no right on these containers (Portainer BE roles).
- Commands on one container run one at a time; two containers never wait for
  each other (a scene that stops web then db stops both). Just before acting,
  Gladys reads the container from Docker: if it cannot, nothing is sent; if
  the container is already running (start) or stopped (stop), nothing is sent
  either. When the command cannot be checked within 3.5 s, nothing is sent
  and Gladys shows a failure (never an action after a failure was shown).
- Docker answers a stop once the container stopped (10 s of grace by
  default). Gladys does not wait that long: it answers "done" at most 4.3 s
  after your command, once the command was sent, and the running state
  follows as soon as Docker is done. A stop or restart asked from Gladys never
  fires the **Container stopped or unhealthy** trigger. Another command on the
  same container is refused while Docker is still at work.
- The containers are recognized by their **name** (and environment), not by
  their Docker id: a container recreated by an image update or by
  `docker compose up` keeps its Gladys device, its history and its scenes.

## Refresh and limits

- The containers (running, health) of every environment are read every 30
  seconds: the running state, the health sensor, the counts and the trigger
  lag by up to 30 seconds.
- The CPU and memory figures cost Docker about a second per container: they
  are read only for the created containers that run, 25 per round at most (3
  at a time; beyond 25, in turn), at the chosen pace. A stopped container
  shows 0. Gladys accepts 300 states per minute from an integration: the CPU
  and memory figures that changed are sent only while this integration has
  sent fewer than 250 in the last minute (the others wait for the next
  round); the running, health and count states are always sent.
- **CPU (%)** is the figure of `docker stats`: 100 means one CPU fully busy
  (400 on four busy CPUs). Gladys has no CPU category: the feature has no
  unit. **Memory** is in MB (10^6 bytes; `docker stats` shows MiB, about 5 %
  less), page cache excluded.
- **Healthy** is published only for a container that has a Docker
  healthcheck (1 healthy, 0 unhealthy; nothing while it is starting).
- The trigger fires when a running container stops (exited or dead) without
  Gladys asking, or when its healthcheck turns unhealthy, once per change,
  with the container, its name, its environment and the problem (`stopped` or
  `unhealthy`). The first reading after a start of the integration fires
  nothing. A container that is removed (not stopped) does not fire.

## Connection problems

- **Token refused** (HTTP 401: wrong, revoked or expired): Gladys does not
  try again by itself, even after a restart. Create a new token, paste it and
  save, or press **Test the connection**.
- **Portainer unreachable**: retried after 30 s, then up to every 10 min; the
  devices show as unreachable meanwhile. An environment that does not answer
  (agent down) only marks its own containers unreachable.
- **Portainer busy** (HTTP 429, met by any request: reading, Discovery,
  command): every request pauses for 1 minute to 6 hours, as long as
  Portainer asks (Retry-After), even across a restart; saving the
  configuration or pressing **Test the connection** lifts it.
- **Certificate changed**: nothing is sent; if you renewed it, press **Trust
  the new certificate** (or type the new fingerprint).

## Limits

- One Portainer per integration, 20 environments and 500 containers at most.
- Docker environments (socket, API or Portainer agent) only: Edge agents
  (their tunnel opens on demand) and Kubernetes are left out.
- Swarm service tasks get a new name at every update: each one becomes a new
  device.
- Not tested with Portainer BE role rules, nor with Podman.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Portainer asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How it works | `section` | No | Gladys reads your Docker containers through the REST API of Portainer (CE or BE 2.x), with an access token. Each container becomes a Gladys device (Discovery tab): running, healthy (healthcheck), CPU and memory, start, stop and restart buttons; each Portainer environment becomes a device with its containers running and stopped. Create the token with a dedicated Portainer user that sees only the environments Gladys needs (see the documentation). Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Portainer.io. |
| Portainer address | `string` | Yes | The address of Portainer on your network: https:\/\/\<IP>:9443. A bare address (no https:\/\/) is read as https on port 9443; with https:\/\/ and no port, port 443 (a reverse proxy, a path is kept). Avoid http:\/\/\<IP>:9000: the token would cross your network in clear. |
| Access token | `secret` | Yes | In Portainer: My account, Access tokens, Add access token. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Portainer, in the X-API-Key header. |
| Certificate | `section` | No | By default the certificate of Portainer must come from a known authority. Portainer generates a self-signed one: either tick the box below (the certificate seen at the first connection is remembered: the token goes to whoever answers that first connection), or type its SHA-256 fingerprint (safer: nothing else is ever accepted, not even the first time). After the first connection, a different certificate is refused before the token is sent. Https only. |
| Accept the self-signed certificate | `boolean` | No | On: the certificate seen at the first connection is trusted and remembered; a different one later is refused until you press "Trust the new certificate". |
| Certificate fingerprint (SHA-256, optional) | `string` | No | Pins this certificate: Portainer must present exactly it. The fingerprint is shown by your browser (certificate details) or by openssl (see the documentation). |
| Environments (optional) | `string` | No | Names or ids of the Portainer environments to follow, separated by commas. Empty: every Docker environment the token sees (Edge and Kubernetes environments are left out). |
| Commands | `section` | No | By default Gladys only reads: the Start, Stop and Restart buttons are refused unless you allow them below (the running state is never a switch: no voice assistant nor "turn everything off" can stop a container). Even then, Gladys never stops nor restarts Gladys itself, its integrations, Portainer, its agent, nor a container connected to the Docker socket. Other vital containers (reverse proxy, DNS, MQTT broker) are not recognized: see the documentation. The user of the token needs the right to operate the containers. |
| Allow starting, stopping and restarting containers | `boolean` | No |  |
| Refresh | `section` | No | Gladys reads the containers (running, health) every 30 seconds. The CPU and memory figures cost more to Docker: they are read at the pace below, only for the containers created in Gladys that run, 25 per round at most. |
| CPU and memory | `select` | Yes |  |

## How to install Portainer in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Portainer appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-portainer:0.1.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-portainer](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-portainer).

Portainer requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Portainer is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
